title: How many outfits can each of them make?
description: {{NAME_1}} has dresses and caps, and {{NAME_2}} has dresses, hats and shoes. The video counts the outfits by branching every choice, and Keeko doubts whether the choices are added or multiplied.
teaching_notes: One idea: each choice pairs with every choice of the next kind, so the counts multiply. Watch for students who add the numbers of dresses, hats and shoes.

source: {{NAME_1}} has 4 dresses and 3 caps. {{NAME_2}} has 7 dresses, 2 hats a
video_script.why: A learner sees that every choice goes with every other choice, so the counts multiply and are not added.
video_script.substitution: the book's own numbers: four dresses and three caps, seven dresses, two hats and three pairs of shoes
video_script.anchor: {{NAME_1}} and {{NAME_2}} choosing clothes from their wardrobes
video_script.wrong_move: adds the numbers of dresses, hats and shoes instead of multiplying them
video_script.payoff_line: Seven dresses, two hats and three pairs of shoes make forty two outfits

final_answer.spoken: twelve outfits and forty two outfits

names.{{NAME_1}}: has four dresses and three caps
names.{{NAME_2}}: has seven dresses, two hats and three pairs of shoes

maths_rules: each of 3 caps goes with each of 4 dresses: 4 + 4 + 4 = 12 = 4 x 3
video_script.design: One idea: choices multiply. Wrong idea: add the choices. Branches grow from one level to three levels, the outfit count only appears at the answer.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; {{NAME_1}} with 4 dresses and 3 caps; {{NAME_2}} with 7 dresses, 2 hats and 3 pairs of shoes

marks.roxie: {{NAME_2}}'s 7 dresses, 2 hats and 3 pairs of shoes appear
marks.ask: an empty box for the outfits appears next to each of them

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This question is from your book.
<bookmark mark='estu'/>{{NAME_1}} has four dresses and three caps.
<bookmark mark='roxie'/>{{NAME_2}} has seven dresses, two hats and three pairs of shoes.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>An outfit takes one of each kind. How many outfits can each of them make?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: one cap with 4 branches to the 4 dresses; the other two caps grow 4 branches each; 4 + 4 + 4 = 4 x 3 = 12

marks.one: one cap grows four branches to the four dresses
marks.all: the other two caps grow four branches each

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Take one cap first. It can go with any of the four dresses, so it gives four outfits.
<bookmark mark='all'/>Each of the other two caps also goes with all four dresses.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>Four plus four plus four is the same as four times three. That is how many outfits {{NAME_1}} has.

beats.on_screen: Given: {{NAME_2}} has 7 dresses, 2 hats, 3 pairs of shoes

marks.given: the three numbers are written on the board

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, {{NAME_2}} has seven dresses, two hats and three pairs of shoes.

beats.on_screen: To find: the number of outfits

marks.find: the words number of outfits are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find how many outfits {{NAME_2}} can make.

beats.on_screen: each of the 7 dresses branches to the 2 hats; 7 x 2 = 14 dress and hat pairs

marks.dress: each of the seven dresses grows two hat branches

narration: <bookmark mark='dress'/>Step one, match each dress with each hat, because every dress goes with both hats.
<bookmark mark='pairs'/>Seven times two gives fourteen dress and hat pairs.

beats.on_screen: each of the 14 pairs branches to the 3 pairs of shoes; 14 x 3

marks.shoes: each of the fourteen pairs grows three shoe branches
marks.times: 14 x 3 is written, the result is left blank

narration: <bookmark mark='shoes'/>Step two, match each pair with each pair of shoes, because every pair goes with all three.
<bookmark mark='times'/>That is fourteen times three.
<bookmark mark='pay'/>Seven dresses, two hats and three pairs of shoes make forty two outfits.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>{{NAME_1}} has twelve outfits and {{NAME_2}} has forty two.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble: 7 + 2 + 3 struck out; one dress with 2 hats and 3 shoes gives 6 outfits

marks.fix: one dress branches to 2 hats and 3 shoes, giving 6 outfits
marks.all: the seven dresses each carry 6 outfits and the bubble is struck out

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks seven plus two plus three gives the outfits, by adding the dresses, hats and shoes.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But adding counts single things, not outfits. One dress alone makes two times three, which is six outfits.
<bookmark mark='all'/>Each of the seven dresses does the same, so the choices are multiplied.
